prompt: Rehearse an upstream update in isolated fixtures, then restore a previous immutable package and its matching inventory through the reviewed rollback procedure.
requirements: Use injected source responses and owned linked Git worktrees under Herd. Execute no upstream program and contact no service.
Exercise a modified leaf, added skill, renamed reference, deleted support file and changed notice through check, prepare, reviewed exact-byte apply and failed validation.
Preserve the portable adaptation and newer destination-only customization, secrets and host settings during failed update, caught interruption and rollback.
Review exhaustive ownership for both immutable package trees, including port-only helpers, and approve the exact computed rollback plan digest separately.
Validate package references, inventory provenance and host evidence. Staging and rollback never establish acceptance.
Reject missing releases, incomplete ownership, stale bytes, unsafe paths and unknown or incompatible runtime-state migrations before replacement.

Passing evidence may name an immutable frozen ancestor only with explicit tested-package provenance proving identical operative bytes, source inventory identity and version; empty acceptance evidence blocks restoration.

Allow explicitly declared post-freeze host reports only at docs/testing/codex.md, docs/testing/chatgpt.md and docs/testing/release-checklist.md; neighboring helper/setup changes remain operative and block stale evidence.
expectedFull: Structural fixture checks pass. The restored package digest and inventory match the immutable release snapshot. Both host behaviors remain unobserved.
expectedReduced: A safe preview identifies unresolved ownership, validation or state compatibility. The existing package remains intact and no rollback or acceptance is claimed.
expectedBlocked: Missing authorization, ownership, release data or compatible state blocks mutation and preserves current package and personal content.
forbiddenClaims: A structural regression proves actual host behavior or release readiness.
An approval flag authenticates a human or grants authorization by itself.
Rollback reverts external automations, user data or installed host settings.
Caught interruption recovery proves power-loss or uncatchable process-termination recovery.
A draft patch or candidate staging receipt establishes acceptance.
